| `@starting-style { ... }`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Provides the initial style used when a native animation or transition begins.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `:first-child` / `:last-child` / `:only-child` / `:nth-child(an+b \| odd \| even)` / `:nth-last-child(...)` / `:nth-child(an+b of <inner>)`                                                                                                                                               | Match by literal JSX position among the parent's direct children. Full `an+b` formula syntax, keyword shortcuts (`odd`, `even`), reverse counting (`nth-last-child`), and selector-filtered child lists via `:nth-child(an+b of S)` and `:nth-last-child(an+b of S)`. The `of S` inner accepts the same simple selectors as `:has(<simple>)` (component reference or single attribute selector); complex inner selectors with combinators fall back to the generic complex-selector warn.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `:first-of-type` / `:last-of-type` / `:only-of-type` / `:nth-of-type(...)` / `:nth-last-of-type(...)`                                                                                                                                                                                     | Like the `:nth-child` family but count only same-element-type siblings (`styled.View` and `styled.Text` are different types).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `--name: value;` declarations and `--name: initial`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Custom property declarations publish through the component cascade so descendants can read them via `var()`. `initial` resets to the guaranteed-invalid value. Trailing `!important` is stripped from custom property values. Bare `--` (no name) is reserved and dropped. Case-sensitive names. (See the `var()` row in the render-time section for substitution semantics.)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `!important` on a declaration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | Within a single styled component, important declarations beat normal ones regardless of source order, across base + matched `@media` / `@container` / `@supports` / attribute / pseudo / `:has()` / `:nth-child()` / combinator buckets. Shorthand `!important` propagates to every longhand. Web-aligned: a styled `!important` beats the runtime `style={{}}` prop; normal declarations don't. `!important` inside `@keyframes` bodies is ignored.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `accent-color: auto \| <color>`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | Tints `styled.Switch`'s on-state surface across iOS, Android, and the web. `auto` resolves to the platform accent color. Wrapping a non-Switch control? Use `.attrs((_props, ast) => ({ tintColor: ast.pop('accentColor') }))` to route the resolved value to whichever prop the wrapped component reads.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `animation` shorthand / longhands                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Supports direction, fill mode, play state, iteration count, easing, delay, and duration for native animations.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `aspect-ratio: auto` / `auto <ratio>`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | Uses the ratio value; development builds warn that the `auto` portion only honors intrinsic dimensions on replaced elements.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Attribute-selector operators (`[attr~=word]` / `[attr\|=prefix]` / `[attr^=]` / `[attr$=]` / `[attr*=]`)                                                                                                                                                                                  | Matches props using CSS word, prefix, suffix, and substring selector semantics.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `background` shorthand                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Supports layered gradients, background color, position, size, and repeat from the CSS shorthand.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `border-inline-*` / `border-block-*` longhands + shorthands + composite + mode-spanning forms                                                                                                                                                                                             | Applies logical border widths and colors in React Native's horizontal writing mode. Per-edge border styles are browser-only; native builds warn and ignore them.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `calc()` / `min()` / `max()` / `clamp()` with static arms                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Resolves static math to a React Native-compatible number or percentage.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `caret-color`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | Android maps the first color to the caret only; iOS lifts the same value as the text-input tint so the caret picks up the color (the selection highlight gets tinted as a side-effect, because iOS exposes a single surface for both); rn-web lets the browser handle it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `corner-shape: round \| squircle \| superellipse()`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Maps `round` to iOS's circular corner curve and `squircle` (and `superellipse()` values near it) to the Apple-smooth continuous curve. Other contours (`bevel`, `notch`, `scoop`, `square`, and out-of-band superellipse values) and corners that mix shapes have no React Native equivalent, so they drop with a one-time development warning. Android renders circular corners regardless and also warns. rn-web passes the value through for browsers that support it (Chrome 139+). Expect a softer difference on iOS than on the web: Apple's continuous curve is a gentler smoothing than the true superellipse the browser draws for the same `squircle` value, so the round-vs-squircle delta is subtle at typical radii.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `color-mix(in <space>, colorA [p%], colorB [p%])` with literal operands                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Mixed in the requested space (`lab`, `lch`, `oklab`, `oklch`, `srgb`) per CSS Color Level 5 and rendered as sRGB hex before it reaches React Native / react-native-web. Perceptual spaces use proper round-trip + shorter-arc hue. Dynamic values resolve at render time.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| CSS system colors (`AccentColor`, `AccentColorText`, `ActiveText`, `ButtonBorder`, `ButtonFace`, `ButtonText`, `Canvas`, `CanvasText`, `Field`, `FieldText`, `GrayText`, `Highlight`, `HighlightText`, `LinkText`, `Mark`, `MarkText`, `SelectedItem`, `SelectedItemText`, `VisitedText`) | Resolve against the OS theme on every target, including forced-colors mode and high-contrast settings on the web. Composite values like `border`, `outline`, `background`, `text-decoration`, `text-shadow`, `box-shadow`, `filter` / `drop-shadow()`, multi-value `border-color`, logical border colors, and two-token `caret-color` accept system keywords in any color slot. A few colors use explicit platform-scoped fallbacks where the platform does not expose the matching semantic: `HighlightText` remains `light-dark()` on native, Android `GrayText` uses a `light-dark()` fallback when theme text-color attrs do not resolve cleanly, Android `SelectedItemText` follows the platform foreground instead of assuming the selected fill is dark, iOS `SelectedItemText` uses white, iOS `MarkText` uses black, and `AccentColorText` uses white. Deprecated CSS Color 4 aliases map to the mandatory keywords.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| CSS Values 4 Math L4 (`abs` / `exp` / `hypot` / inverse trig / `log` / `mod` / `pow` / `rem` / `round` / `sign` / `sqrt` / trig) with static arms                                                                                                                                         | Resolves static math functions to React Native-compatible values.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `field-sizing: content`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Auto-grows a `styled.TextInput` to its content height. Author-declared `min-height` / `max-height` still bound the growth. Explicit `multiline={false}` disables the auto-grow behavior and warns in development. On rn-web, the input renders as a `<textarea>` and the browser handles `field-sizing` where supported.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `flex` / `flex-flow` shorthands                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | Supports the CSS shorthand syntax for React Native flex grow, shrink, basis, direction, and wrapping behavior.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `font-size: <absolute-size> \| <relative-size> \| <length-percentage>`                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Keyword sizes (`xx-small`…`xxx-large`) resolve to a fixed pixel ramp on every platform. `larger` / `smaller` adjust against the cascade font-size (next entry on the ramp, otherwise ×1.2 or ÷1.2). Absolute lengths (`pt`, `pc`, `in`, `cm`, `mm`, `Q`) fold to dp at compile time. Percentages, font-relative units (`em` / `rem` / `lh` / `rlh` plus the font-metric forms `ex` / `cap` / `ch` / `ic` and their `r`-variants), viewport units (`vh` / `vw` / `dvh` / `svh` / `lvh` and width counterparts), and container-query units (`cqh` / `cqw` / `cqi` / `cqb` / `cqmin` / `cqmax`) defer to the cascade resolver so they track the current environment.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `font-style: oblique <angle>`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | Maps to `italic` on native (angle dropped + warned); rn-web honors the slant axis natively.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Generic `font-family` keywords (`cursive`, `emoji`, `fangsong`, `fantasy`, `math`, `monospace`, `sans-serif`, `serif`, `system-ui`, `ui-*`)                                                                                                                                               | Uses an appropriate platform font on iOS and Android; comma-separated fallback lists keep the first family and warn in development.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `hyphens: none \| manual \| auto`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Android maps to the system hyphenation frequency; rn-web lets the browser handle it; iOS keeps manual soft-hyphen behavior and warns for `auto`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `interactivity: inert`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Blocks pointer interaction, hides the subtree from assistive technology where React Native exposes that control, and disables focus, text selection, and editing on the styled component. rn-web uses the browser's `inert` behavior.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `letter-spacing: <length> \| <number> \| normal`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Numbers and px values resolve at compile time. Absolute lengths fold to dp. Font-relative, viewport, and container-query units defer to the cascade resolver. `normal` is `0`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `line-height: <length-percentage> \| <number> \| normal`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | Unitless multipliers and px values resolve at compile time. Absolute lengths (`pt`, `pc`, `in`, `cm`, `mm`, `Q`) fold to dp. Percentages map to the equivalent `em` ratio. Font-relative units (`em` / `rem` / `lh` / `rlh` plus font-metric forms `ex` / `cap` / `ch` / `ic` and their `r`-variants), viewport units, and container-query units defer to the cascade resolver.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `linear()` easing                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Supports piecewise-linear easing for native animations and transitions.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `line-clamp: N`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | Limits text-like components to the requested number of lines and clips overflow.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `margin-inline` / `margin-block` / `padding-inline` / `padding-block` / `inset-inline` / `inset-block` shorthands                                                                                                                                                                         | Supports the logical shorthand syntax in React Native's horizontal writing mode.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `oklch()`, `oklab()`, `lch()`, `lab()` with static channels                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Converted to sRGB hex before reaching React Native / react-native-web.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `outline` shorthand                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Supports CSS outline width, style, and color shorthand syntax.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `overscroll-behavior`, `overscroll-behavior-x`, `overscroll-behavior-y`, `overscroll-behavior-inline`, `overscroll-behavior-block`: `auto \| contain \| none \| chain`                                                                                                                    | On native maps to `bounces` / `overScrollMode` on `styled.ScrollView`; web honors the value natively.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `perspective` standalone property                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Applies perspective through the component's transform.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `round(line-width, A)`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Snaps A to the device pixel grid at render time using the platform's pixel ratio per the "snap a length as a line width" algorithm. Useful for hairline borders that should align to physical pixels regardless of screen scale.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `place-content` / `place-items` / `place-self` shorthands                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Supports CSS alignment shorthand syntax for React Native's flex alignment surfaces. The justify-items / justify-self half is browser-only and has no effect on iOS or Android.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `scrollbar-width: auto \| thin \| none`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | On native, `none` hides ScrollView indicators; web honors `auto` and `thin` natively.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `scroll-snap-type: none \| [ x \| y \| block \| inline \| both ] [ mandatory \| proximity ]?`                                                                                                                                                                                             | On native, children of a styled scroller declaring `scroll-snap-align` define real snap positions: the scroll container measures them and derives `snapToOffsets` (start / center / end alignment, mixed sizes welcome), and `scroll-snap-stop: always` on a child prevents a fling from skipping past it. With no aligned children, `mandatory` falls back to full-scrollport paging (`pagingEnabled` plus fast `decelerationRate`); size each slide to the scrollport in that mode, since paging advances in scrollport-width steps. A settle guarantee watches mandatory scrollers and animates any off-grid rest to the nearest snap point (Android's engine can otherwise strand a caught snap). RN has no proximity engine, so bare-axis / `proximity` apply fast deceleration only; both forms warn once in development. Pass `snapToInterval` or `snapToOffsets` on the ScrollView for precise snap points (those props win over the approximation). Web honors `scroll-snap-type` natively. Android quirk: tapping to catch an in-flight snap animation and lifting without dragging leaves the scroller resting between snap points; React Native's emulated snap engine cancels the snap on touch-down and only re-snaps after a drag, while iOS re-snaps natively on every release. |
| Relative color syntax (`rgb(from <color> ...)`, `hsl(from <color> ...)`, `hwb(from <color> ...)`, `color(from <color> <space> ...)`, `oklch(from <color> ...)`, `oklab(from <color> ...)`, `lch(from <color> ...)`, `lab(from <color> ...)`)                                              | Rendered as an sRGB color React Native can display when the base color is knowable, including literal colors, modern color functions, and resolved theme values. The legacy comma-separated form is not valid in relative syntax (per spec) and is dropped with a warning. `currentColor` bases warn and drop on native because React Native cannot resolve them from inherited styles.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `text-overflow: clip \| ellipsis \| <string> \| fade \| fade()`                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | Truncates on every target when paired with `line-clamp` or `text-wrap: nowrap` so the content has somewhere to overflow. On native maps onto `<Text>`'s `ellipsizeMode`. The Level 4 forms approximate on native (a string renders as an ellipsis, `fade` clips, and two-value forms use the end value) with a one-time development warning; rn-web passes the full grammar through to the browser.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `text-shadow` shorthand and multi-shadow lists                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Folds the shorthand onto React Native text shadows. React Native renders a single shadow per Text, so a comma-separated list applies the first (topmost) layer with a one-time development warning; stack duplicate Text elements to layer more. On web the browser renders the full list.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `text-wrap: [ wrap \| nowrap ] \|\| [ auto \| balance \| stable \| pretty ]`                                                                                                                                                                                                              | `nowrap` renders as one clipped line. `balance` and `pretty` use Android text breaking controls; iOS keeps default line breaking and warns. `stable` is preserved but ignored on native with a warning.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `text-wrap-mode: wrap \| nowrap`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Supports the mode portion of `text-wrap` independently.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `text-wrap-style: auto \| balance \| stable \| pretty`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Supports the style portion of `text-wrap` independently, with the same platform limits as `text-wrap`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `transform-box`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | Ignored on iOS / Android with a one-time development warning because React Native transforms use the view center as their reference box. Use `transform-origin` to move the pivot. rn-web keeps `transform-box` for the browser.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `transition` shorthand / longhands                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Animates supported property changes automatically; reduced-motion settings collapse durations to zero.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `vertical-align: top \| middle \| bottom \| auto`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Android maps through to RN's text vertical alignment; rn-web maps top/middle/bottom to content alignment while preserving other browser values; iOS warns because RN has no text vertical-align API there.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

### Dynamic polyfills

These values re-resolve each render against the component tree or the device's current state. Components that don't use any of them pay zero cost.

| Feature                                                                       | What to expect                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `@container`, `container-type`, and `container-name`                          | Container queries use the measured size of the nearest or named styled container.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `animation-timeline: scroll()` + `scroll-timeline` + `animation-range`        | Scroll-driven animations: keyframe progress follows the scroll position of the nearest (or named) styled scroll container instead of a clock. `animation-range` restricts the active slice (percentages, lengths, mixed `calc()`). Named timelines (`scroll-timeline-name` on the scroller, `animation-timeline: --name` on descendants) resolve through the ancestor chain. `animation-timeline: view()` drives keyframes from the subject's own visibility: progress runs from the subject entering the scrollport to it leaving, with the named ranges (`cover`, `contain`, `entry`, `exit`, `entry-crossing`, `exit-crossing`, `scroll`) usable in `animation-range`. View subjects must be direct children of the styled scroll container; `view-timeline-inset` is ignored with a dev warning. `scroll(root)`, `scroll(self)`, and infinite iteration counts are inactive with a dev warning. Requires the default Animated adapter (Reanimated CSS layer is time-based). |
| `anchor-name` + `anchor()` + `anchor-size()`                                  | Anchor positioning: an element declares `anchor-name: --x` and absolutely positioned siblings bind their `top` / `left` insets to its edges (`top: anchor(--x bottom)`) and their sizes to its box (`width: anchor-size(--x width)`), composing inside `calc()`. The element and its anchor must share a parent; `bottom` / `right` insets and the logical side keywords are not mapped yet and use the declared fallback. On web the browser handles anchor positioning natively.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `@property`                                                                   | Registered custom properties: `syntax`, `inherits`, and `initial-value` descriptors apply to `var()` resolution. Unset registered properties resolve to their typed initial value, and `inherits: false` properties ignore ancestor declarations (descendants see the initial value). Supported syntax strings: `*`, `<length>`, `<number>`, `<percentage>`, `<integer>`, `<angle>`, `<time>`, `<color>`; invalid rules warn and are ignored per spec. On web the registration forwards to the browser's `CSS.registerProperty()`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `position: sticky`                                                            | Direct styled children of a styled ScrollView stick to the top edge by rendering a layout-pinned twin in an overlay above the scroller: the stuck position is fixed by layout (nothing updates per frame, so it holds through flings), and visibility hands off between the in-flow original and the pinned twin at the crossover via complementary UI-thread opacity interpolations. Top-edge only, direct children only, and inset offsets (`top: 8px`) are not applied. Multiple sticky siblings stick independently and overlap; there is no push-off between consecutive headers. Component state inside a sticky element is not shared between its two renders, and the overlay aligns to the scroller's frame without subtracting the scroller's own border widths. On web the browser handles sticky itself.                                                                                                                                                            |
| `display: grid` (fixed equal columns)                                         | A `display: grid` container with `grid-template-columns: repeat(N, 1fr)` (or an equal `1fr` track list) plus `gap` / `row-gap` / `column-gap` lays out direct styled children into N equal columns; the container measures its width and each child sizes itself to its share. `grid-column: span N` spans N columns. Direct styled children only (the spec's grid items); the container falls back to a wrapping flex row before its first measurement. Fixed px tracks, `minmax()`, `auto`, `auto-fill` / `auto-fit`, unequal `fr` factors, line-number / named-line placement, `grid-row`, `grid-area`, and non-`row` `grid-auto-flow` are not supported and warn. On web the browser lays out the full grid.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `attr(name <type>?, fallback?)` (CSS Values 5)                                | Reads the styled component's props (the same source attribute selectors match), so `width: attr(data-size px, 48px)` sizes from a `data-size` prop. Supports the `number` keyword, unit names (`px`, `%`, `deg`, ...), `raw-string`, and `type(*)` / `type(<length>)` / `type(<number>)` / `type(<percentage>)` / `type(<color>)`. Missing props and type mismatches use the fallback; dynamic fallbacks (`light-dark()`, viewport units, math) resolve too.
