Composes inside `calc()`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `background-blend-mode`                                                       | On iOS / Android, layered backgrounds render with React Native primitives; rn-web lets the browser handle it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `cqw` / `cqh` / `cqmin` / `cqmax` / `cqi` / `cqb`                             | Nearest registered container's `onLayout` size.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `em` / `lh` / `rlh` length units                                              | Resolve against inherited font size and line height, so typography-based spacing follows the cascade on native.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `env(safe-area-inset-top \| right \| bottom \| left)`                         | `useSafeAreaInsets()` (SafeAreaProvider context).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `light-dark(light, dark)`                                                     | `Appearance.getColorScheme()`; swaps when OS theme changes.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `rem` length unit                                                             | `1rem` = 16px by default; `createTheme({ rootFontSize: N })` rescales the ramp. Composes inside `calc()` alongside other static arms.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `sibling-index()` / `sibling-count()` (CSS Values 5 tree counting)            | 1-indexed position among the parent styled component's children and the total child count, usable anywhere an integer works and inside `calc()` (`width: calc(sibling-index() * 10px)`). Re-resolve live when siblings mount, unmount, or reorder. An element whose parent is not a styled component resolves as an only child (1 of 1).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `text-align: start \| end \| match-parent`                                    | Resolves to left or right from the current inherited `direction`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `var(--name, fallback?)` (CSS Custom Properties Module Level 1)               | Resolves against `--*` declarations on any ancestor styled component (nearer wins), with fallbacks, nested resolution, and cycle detection. `var(--path)` from `createTheme(...)` leaves still resolves through the active `ThemeProvider`. Works in base declarations, inside `@media` / `@container` / `@supports` blocks, inside attribute selectors, and inside pseudo-class blocks. Quoted strings inside the fallback preserve any literal `)` or `,` characters.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `vw` / `vh` / `vmin` / `vmax` / `dvh` / `svh` / `lvh` / `dvw` / `svw` / `lvw` | `Dimensions.get('window')` (re-measures on rotation / resize).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

### React Native pseudo-states (equivalent to CSS pseudo-classes)

Interaction pseudo-states resolve through the live state React Native provides, which only `Pressable` (or a custom component forwarding its style to one) supplies. On other elements (`View`, `Text`, etc.) the base styles still apply but the pseudo buckets stay inert with a one-time development warning, since those hosts have no press / hover / focus state to track. A bucket fenced behind a non-matching media query (e.g. web-only `@media (hover: hover)` rules) stays silent.

| CSS                      | React Native mapping                                                                             |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `&:active` / `&:pressed` | `Pressable` pressed state.                                                                       |
| `&:disabled`             | Component `disabled` prop.                                                                       |
| `&:focus` / `&:focused`  | `onFocus`/`onBlur` on focusable inputs.                                                          |
| `&:hover`                | `Pressable` hover state (desktop / web) or `onHoverIn`/`onHoverOut` (iOS pencil / desktop-like). |

### Image and ImageBackground

- **`Image`**: authored layout and paint (`width`, `height`, `margin`, `opacity`, `borderRadius`, `tintColor`, `resizeMode` / `objectFit`, filters and shadows on the view) map to RN `Image` / wrapper styles like any other view-backed component.
- **`ImageBackground`**: the outer container accepts normal **view** styles (positioning, flex, padding). The bitmap layer uses React Native’s **`imageStyle`** (or equivalent) for `resizeMode`, `borderRadius` on the image, `tintColor`, and background image sizing; layered CSS `background` from templates may split between **container** and **image** styles after compilation. Prefer explicit layout on the wrapper when you need predictable clipping or padding around the image.

### TextInput, Switch, and Button (style vs props)

- **`TextInput`**: treat **box model**, **typography**, **colors**, **outline**, and **opacity** as normal template CSS when they map to RN style keys. **Placeholder text and color**, **caret / selection colors**, **keyboard type**, **secure text entry**, **return key behavior**, **autocorrect**, **multiline** scrolling, and similar controls are **React props** (or platform-specific props), not something to spell as non-standard CSS in templates. Some real CSS (for example `caret-color`) may map to RN props where the platform exposes them; see the polyfilled and native rows above when listed.
- **`Switch`**: **track and thumb colors**, **disabled** state, and iOS background tint are **props**. Layout around the control (margins, flex alignment) is **style** on the same component or a parent `View`.
- **`Button`**: RN’s `Button` is not a general-purpose styled surface. For CSS-shaped controls, compose **`Pressable` (or `Touchable*`) plus `Text`** so template CSS applies to ordinary view and text children.

## Not yet supported (compatibility tracker)

These features depend on upstream React Native primitives that do not yet exist. Each row lists what's missing, the workaround we recommend today, and (where known) the upstream request to follow or support. When a row ships in a React Native release, we'll wire it up and move it out of this section.

### Layout & positioning

| Feature                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Why unsupported                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | Workaround                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Anchor positioning beyond the same-parent inset subset: `anchor-scope`, `position-area`, `position-try`, `position-try-fallbacks`, `position-try-order`, `position-visibility`, `@position-try`, `bottom` / `right` / logical-side `anchor()` insets                            | No CSS-level anchor positioning primitive on RN; only the same-parent `anchor-name` + `position-anchor` + `anchor()` / `anchor-size()` inset subset is polyfilled (see Dynamic polyfills above). See [CSS Anchor Positioning](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-anchor-position-1/).                                                                                                                                                                                  | Use the supported anchor subset, popover libraries, or `Modal` + measured coordinates.                  |
| `display: flow-root`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | No block-formatting-context concept on RN.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Use a plain `View`.                                                                                     |
| CSS Grid beyond the fixed-equal-columns subset: variable / `minmax()` / `auto` / `auto-fill` / `auto-fit` tracks, `grid-template-rows`, `grid-template-areas`, line-number / named-line placement, `grid-row`, `grid-area`, non-`row` `grid-auto-flow`, `subgrid`, masonry axes | React Native 0.85 exposes no grid layout style props; only the equal-`1fr`-columns subset is polyfilled (see Dynamic polyfills above).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | Use the supported `display: grid` subset, flexbox, nested `View`s, or `FlatList` with multiple columns. |
| `position: fixed`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | React Native has no top-layer / viewport-anchored positioning primitive.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Use `Modal` or a portal-style overlay component.                                                        |
| `position: sticky` beyond the top-edge subset                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | The polyfill pins direct styled children of a styled ScrollView against the top edge (see Dynamic polyfills above). Side / bottom edges, inset offsets, push-off between consecutive headers, and nested (non-direct) sticky elements are not implemented.                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Use the supported subset or `FlatList` sticky headers.                                                  |
| CSS-wide keywords (`initial` / `inherit` / `unset` / `revert` / `revert-layer`)                                                                                                                                                                                                 | React Native has no cascade to resolve them against, and its style defaults differ from CSS initial values (for example `flex-direction`), so a silent drop would invert author intent. Native drops the declaration with a one-time development warning; rn-web passes it through to the browser. Exceptions that keep working: `direction: inherit` (React Native implements it natively) and `flex: initial` (expanded statically per the Flexbox shorthand). | Set an explicit value.                                                                                  |
| `order`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | React Native's Yoga renders children in JSX order; there is no visual reordering primitive. Native drops the declaration with a one-time development warning; rn-web passes it through.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Reorder the JSX children, or use `flex-direction: row-reverse` / `column-reverse`.                      |
| `reading-flow` / `reading-order`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | RN's accessibility model uses `accessibilityRole` / focus traversal, not CSS.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Use `accessibilityElementsHidden` / `importantForAccessibility`.                                        |

### Colors & rendering

| Feature                                                                                       | Why unsupported                                                                                                                                                             | Workaround                                                                                                                    |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `@media (color-gamut: srgb \| p3 \| rec2020)`                                                 | No color-space capability query on RN.                                                                                                                                      | Assume sRGB; re-evaluate if wide-gamut support lands upstream.                                                                |
| `@media (dynamic-range: standard \| high)` / `@media (video-dynamic-range: standard \| high)` | No HDR capability query on RN.                                                                                                                                              | Branch on other signals (explicit user toggle, platform API).                                                                 |
| `@media (forced-colors: none \| active)`                                                      | High-contrast mode is Windows-only on web; no RN equivalent.                                                                                                                | Use RN's `AccessibilityInfo.isHighTextContrastEnabled()` where available.                                                     |
| `background-image: url(...)` without a blend-mode polyfill path                               | React Native's native background-image parser handles gradients, not image URLs.                                                                                            | Render an `Image` / `ImageBackground`, or use `background-blend-mode` when a blended background layer is the intended effect. |
| `backdrop-filter`                                                                             | No native backdrop-blur primitive on RN.                                                                                                                                    | Use `BlurView` from `@react-native-community/blur` or Skia.                                                                   |
| `border-style: double`                                                                        | Only `solid`, `dashed`, `dotted` supported.                                                                                                                                 | Use a nested border + inner padding.                                                                                          |
| `color-contrast()`                                                                            | Needs rendered-color analysis primitive; only shipped in Safari today.                                                                                                      | Tune an `oklch` lightness threshold manually or select colors via a theme helper.                                             |
| `conic-gradient()` / `repeating-conic-gradient()`                                             | React Native's gradient parser covers linear and radial only. A conic layer renders nothing on native and emits a one-time development warning; it still renders on rn-web. | Use a `linear-gradient` / `radial-gradient`, a prebaked image, or Skia for custom paint.                                      |

### Typography & text

| Feature                                                                                               | Why unsupported                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Workaround                                                                  |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `@font-palette-values` (`font-family`, `base-palette: light \| dark \| <integer>`, `override-colors`) | Color font palette descriptors are not exposed by RN.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Use multiple font files keyed by palette.                                   |
| `font-palette: normal \| light \| dark \| <palette-identifier> \| palette-mix(...)`                   | Color font palette selection is not exposed by RN.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Use multiple font files keyed by palette.                                   |
| `font-synthesis: none \| [ weight \|\| style \|\| small-caps \|\| position ]`                         | No control over synthetic font generation.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Link the real weight variants in your native build.                         |
| `hanging-punctuation`                                                                                 | Safari-only on web; not implemented on RN.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Manual layout tweaks.                                                       |
| `initial-letter`                                                                                      | Drop-cap primitive missing.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | Render the first letter as a separate sized component.                      |
| `line-break: auto \| loose \| normal \| strict \| anywhere`                                           | East-Asian line-breaking rules missing.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Use a CJK-aware text component when needed.                                 |
| `text-box-trim` / `text-box-edge`                                                                     | `Text` can't measure glyph metrics.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Adjust `line-height` and vertical padding manually.                         |
| `aspect-ratio: auto <ratio>` on image-like components                                                 | React Native exposes no natural-aspect-ratio surface, so the specified ratio applies even where CSS prefers the image's natural ratio. Plain views match the spec exactly (the specified ratio is the defined behavior for non-replaced boxes).                                       | Use `aspect-ratio: auto` alone to keep an image's natural ratio.            |
| `text-decoration-color` on Android                                                                    | Android paints underlines and strike-throughs in the text color; React Native exposes no per-decoration color there. iOS and rn-web honor the authored color. Native warns once in development when a color is authored.                                                              | Match the text color, or put a `border-bottom` on a wrapping View.          |
| `text-decoration-style: wavy`                                                                         | Wavy decoration is not exposed by RN.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Use a custom underline view if needed.                                      |
| `text-decoration-thickness` / `text-underline-offset` / `text-underline-position`                     | React Native draws a fixed-position, fixed-weight underline with no thickness, offset, or position control. Native drops these with a one-time development warning (the `text-decoration` shorthand still applies the line / style / color it can parse); rn-web passes them through. | Put a `border-bottom` on a wrapping View for a heavier or offset underline. |
| `text-wrap-style: avoid-orphans`                                                                      | No orphan-avoidance line breaking control on RN.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | Split text manually at known break points.                                  |
| `word-spacing`                                                                                        | `Text` doesn't expose word-spacing.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Accept default; use `letter-spacing` if similar effect helps.               |

### Animations & transitions

| Feature                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Why unsupported                                                                                                                                                            | Workaround                                                             |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `@view-transition`, `view-transition-name`, `view-transition-class`, `view-transition-group`, `view-transition-scope`                                                                                              | Single-view architecture; View Transition pseudo-element capture does not apply. See [CSS View Transitions](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-view-transitions-1/).             | Use screen-transition animations via `React Navigation`.               |
| Scroll-driven timelines beyond the polyfilled subset: `scroll(root)` / `scroll(self)`, named view timelines (`view-timeline`, `view-timeline-name`, `view-timeline-axis`), `view-timeline-inset`, `timeline-scope` | No scroll-driven animation timeline primitive on RN; the polyfill covers `scroll()` / `view()` / named scroll timelines + `animation-range` (see Dynamic polyfills above). | Use a `ScrollView` `onScroll` listener + `Animated.Value.interpolate`. |

### Scrolling & interaction

| Feature                                                             | Why unsupported                             | Workaround                                     |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `resize: none \| both \| horizontal \| vertical \| block \| inline` | No resize-handle primitive.                 | Build a custom drag handle with pan gestures.  |
| `scroll-behavior: smooth`                                           | Not CSS-mappable on RN.                     | Use `ScrollView.scrollTo({ animated: true })`. |
| `scroll-padding`, `scroll-margin`                                   | Depends on full scroll-snap support.        | Inline offsets in `contentContainerStyle`.     |
| `touch-action` (CSS)                                                | RN gesture handlers handle this implicitly. | Configure `Pressable`/`GestureHandler` props.  |

### Selectors that depend on the DOM

| Feature                                                                                          | Why unsupported                                                                                                                              | Workaround                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `:defined`                                                                                       | No custom-element registry on RN.                                                                                                            | N/A.                                                                           |
| `:dir(ltr \| rtl)`                                                                               | No `writing-mode` support on RN.                                                                                                             | Branch on `I18nManager.isRTL`.                                                 |
| `:empty`                                                                                         | Children-count introspection isn't published in `ParentContext`.                                                                             | Branch on the prop or render the empty case as a separate component.           |
| `:has()` with complex inner                                                                      | The simple-inner form (`:has(${Component})`, `:has([attr])`) is supported; descendant chains and combinator selectors inside `:has` are not. | Restructure to a single simple-inner predicate; multiple `:has` rules compose. |
| `:popover-open`, `:modal`, `:fullscreen`                                                         | No equivalent RN states.                                                                                                                     | Use component state.                                                           |
| `:target`                                                                                        | No URL fragment routing on RN.                                                                                                               | Branch on route params.                                                        |
| Form-state pseudos `:checked`, `:required`, `:user-valid`, `:user-invalid`, `:placeholder-shown` | Form semantics differ on RN.                                                                                                                 | Use component state.                                                           |

### At-rules

| Feature                   | Why unsupported                                                                         | Workaround                                                                               |
| ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `@layer` (cascade layers) | The native cascade is positional (nearer ancestor wins) and lacks named layer ordering. | Use explicit style order in your components, or `!important` for in-component overrides. |
| `@scope`                  | No selector scoping on RN.                                                              | Use component composition.                                                               |
| `@supports selector(...)` | No selector feature registry.                                                           | Branch on explicit feature checks.                                                       |

### Environment variables

| Feature                                                  | Why unsupported                                      | Workaround                                            |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `@media (prefers-reduced-data: no-preference \| reduce)` | No browser implementation yet.                       | Branch on explicit data-saver preference in your app. |
| `env(keyboard-inset-*)`                                  | Keyboard inset env variables are web-only currently. | Use `Keyboard.addListener` events.                    |
| `env(titlebar-area-*)`                                   | Desktop PWA concept.                                 | Not applicable to mobile RN.                          |
| `env(viewport-segment-*)` (foldable / dual-screen)       | No foldable API on RN.                               | Use device-specific APIs.                             |

## Routing values onto wrapped components with `attrs`

Some CSS properties only target a specific React Native primitive on native: `text-overflow` and the line-clamp surface drive props on `<Text>`; `accent-color` drives `<Switch>`; `overscroll-behavior`, `scrollbar-width`, and `scroll-snap-type` drive `<ScrollView>` props. The default polyfill lifts the right props automatically when you style one of those primitives directly.

When you wrap a third-party component instead (e.g. a Slider, Checkbox, ProgressBar, BottomSheet), you can route the resolved CSS value onto whatever prop the wrapped component expects using the function form of `.attrs(...)` with the AST bridge. The second argument exposes `peek(key)` (read) and `pop(key)` (read and consume).

```tsx
import Slider from '@react-native-community/slider';
import styled from 'styled-components/native';

const ThemedSlider = styled(Slider).attrs<{ thumbTintColor?: string }>((_props, ast) => ({
  thumbTintColor: ast.pop('accentColor') as string | undefined,
}))`
  accent-color: red;
`;
```

`pop('accentColor')` returns the resolved value (a string, a theme token, or a `PlatformColor` for `accent-color: auto`) and removes it from the style bag so it doesn't end up as an unrecognized style key on the wrapped component. Use `peek` if you also need the value to stay in the style. The same pattern works with any CSS property: write the standards-compliant declaration in the template, route the value onto whichever prop the wrapped component actually reads.

## Contributing

If you spot a feature missing from this list, or a workaround that's out of date, open a pull request against this file. When upstream React Native ships a primitive that lets us move a row out of the unsupported section, the same PR should update the polyfill layer so the capability becomes available in styled-components immediately.

# Tips and tricks

Source: https://github.com/styled-components/styled-components/blob/main/packages/styled-components/docs/tips-and-tricks.md

# Tips and tricks

A collection of useful tips and tricks when working with `styled-components`!

## Component adjustments

Say you have a `<Button>` that has a `padding` of `0.5em 2em`:

```JS
const Button = styled.button`
  padding: 0.5em 2em;

  /* …more styles here… */
`;
```

Now your designer has added a new comment section to your articles, and they want the buttons in that section to be smaller than the regular ones.

Using interpolated functions, adjusting the button size is easy as pie. Prefix props you don't want passed to the DOM with `$` (transient props):

```JS
const Button = styled.button`
  /* If it's a small button use less padding */
  padding: ${props => props.$small ? '0.25em 1em' : '0.5em 2em'};

  /* …more styles here… */
`;
```

Then, in your comment section, you can simply say that the `<Button>` should be small:

```JSX
<Button>This is a normal button!</Button>
<Button $small>This is a small button!</Button>
```

## Using JavaScript to our advantage

To make a line overflow with an ellipsis (`…`) when the text is longer than the container element is wide, you need three CSS properties:

```CSS
.truncate {
  white-space: nowrap;
  overflow: hidden;
  text-overflow: ellipsis;
}
```

The width of the container element also needs to be set explicitly:

```CSS
.truncate {
  /* Needs to be specific width */
  width: 250px;
  white-space: nowrap;
  overflow: hidden;
  text-overflow: ellipsis;
}
```

You could create a separate component for truncating, but in this case reusing the CSS might not be a bad idea! Instead of hardcoding those lines of code in every component you want to truncate though, you could write a function that does it for you:

```JS
// style-utils.js
export function truncate(width) {
  return `
    width: ${width};
    white-space: nowrap;
    overflow: hidden;
    text-overflow: ellipsis;
  `;
}
```

Then you can use it like this:

```JSX
import { truncate } from '../style-utils';

// Make this div truncate the text with an ellipsis
const Box = styled.div`
  ${ truncate('250px') }
  background: papayawhip;
`;
```

Does this remind you of anything? Exactly, this is kind of like a mixin in Sass, except it's not an arbitrarily added construct on top of CSS, it's just JavaScript! 👍

## More powerful example

One of the more powerful features of Sass mixins is `@content`, which works a bit like passing `props.children` to a React component, except for CSS:

```scss
@mixin handheld {
  @media (max-width: 420px) {
    @content;
  }
}

.box {
  font-size: 16px;
  @include handheld {
    font-size: 14px;
  }
}
```

Now we have javascript, we can do 🌟 _more powerful things_ 🌟

```js
// style-utils.js
import { css } from 'styled-components';

export const media = {
  handheld: (...args) => css`
    @media (max-width: 420px) {
      ${css(...args)};
    }
  `,
};
```

```js
import { media } from '../style-utils';

// Make the text smaller on handheld devices
const Box = styled.div`
  font-size: 16px;
  ${media.handheld`
    font-size: 14px;
  `};
`;
```

And voila! 💅

_Not clear on why `css` is needed in the above example? Check the article on [Tagged Template Literals](https://styled-components.com/docs/advanced#tagged-template-literals)_

### Media Templates

Due to the functional nature of javascript, you can easily define your own tagged template literal to wrap styles in media queries. For example:

```js
// these sizes are arbitrary and you can set them to whatever you wish
import { css } from 'styled-components';

const sizes = {
  giant: 1170,
  desktop: 992,
  tablet: 768,
  phone: 376,
};

// iterate through the sizes and create a media template
export const media = Object.keys(sizes).reduce((accumulator, label) => {
  // use em in breakpoints to work properly cross-browser and support users
  // changing their browsers font-size: https://zellwk.com/blog/media-query-units/
  const emSize = sizes[label] / 16;
  accumulator[label] = (...args) => css`
    @media (max-width: ${emSize}em) {
      ${css(...args)};
    }
  `;
  return accumulator;
}, {});
```

Great! Now that you've defined your media templates, you can use them like this:

```js
const Container = styled.div`
  color: #333;
  ${media.desktop`padding: 0 20px;`}
  ${media.tablet`padding: 0 10px;`}
  ${media.phone`padding: 0 5px;`}
`;
```

Pretty easy, huh?

### Refs to DOM nodes

styled-components uses React's [`forwardRef`](https://react.dev/reference/react/forwardRef) under the hood. Set refs like you would on any other component and they will automatically resolve to the underlying DOM element or wrapped component class instance.

```JSX
const StyledInput = styled.input`
  color: paleviolet;
`;

class Form extends Component {
  inputRef = React.createRef()

  componentDidMount() {
    if (this.inputRef) {
      this.inputRef.current.focus()
    }
  }

  render() {
    return (
      <StyledInput ref={this.inputRef} />
    )
  }
}
```
